text: We are fighting for the Cyrillic alphabet to be associated with Bulgaria, Albena Spasova told BTA (04.05.2026 17:27)

We are fighting for the Cyrillic alphabet to be associated with Bulgaria beyond the popular idea that we are talking about a Russian alphabet due to the large population of Russia, as well as fighting to create our own fonts. It was really important that the Cyrillic alphabet became one of the three official scripts of Europe precisely through Bulgaria, accepting Bulgaria into the European Union. This was told to BTA by Albena Spassova, a lecturer at the National Academy of Arts (NAA), who on April 22 gave a lecture in Mexico related to the project "The Letters of Bulgaria - The Alphabet of Europe". According to her, the presentation was structured as a "walk through the history of the world poster", including 30 authors with a leading position in this field. "I had constructed the lecture in such a way that it contained an introductory part for the entire project, and then for each of the authors - two slides, in which, in addition to the poster for the project, between three and five of their iconic posters were arranged," Spassova explained. She added that within 60 minutes, a “concise but very interesting presentation” was presented, which has already been published on the website of the International Triennial of the Stage Poster. According to her, the sustained interest in the project is due to both the universal language of the poster and the theme of the Cyrillic alphabet. “The letter has always been a challenge for the poster artist… this is another opportunity to enrich the poster language,” the curator noted. She emphasized that the collection contains “the color of the world poster,” with the works of the participants being part of major international museums.

The participation in Mexico is part of a large-scale international festival in which Bulgaria was the focus. In addition to the exhibition, there were also expositions dedicated to Bulgarian cultural heritage, rose oil and tourism. Within the framework of the event, the Bulgarian artist Grady Assa was awarded the title of "International Honorary Professor".

Albena Spasova noted that the event opens up opportunities for future collaboration, including the participation of Bulgarian students in international initiatives in the field of poster and photography. She also emphasized the role of the Bulgarian Embassy in the implementation of the project, describing the presentation as “glamorous and very impressive.”

The international poster campaign “The Letters of Bulgaria – Alphabet of Europe”, created by the International Triennial of the Stage Poster in 2007, unites 30 artists from 20 countries around the idea of ​​visually presenting the Bulgarian alphabet as one of the three scripts in Europe. The collection includes 30 posters – one for each letter, determined by lot during the fifth edition of the triennial in Sofia. The project combines the creative efforts of established world poster artists and Bulgarian authors, with one of the letters – “Л” – being created after a competition among young Bulgarian artists. All works are realized in a single format and typography and are printed in several languages ​​in a limited edition. The initiative aims to popularize Bulgarian culture through contemporary art, transforming the letters into a universal visual code. The collection has been presented in a number of international cultural centers.
